claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me start with a few questions:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex? For example, does he live with you, or do you pay towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is important - when a child doesn't live with you, the amount you contribute matters for Child Benefit eligibility.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week? And do you know the current weekly Child Benefit rate (which is around £25.60 for the eldest/only child and £16.95 for additional children)?**

To qualify for Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else, you generally need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £10 a week towards his upkeep - for things like clothes and bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I need to understand the living arrangement a bit more:

**How long has Alex been living away from you? And is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because the rules differ depending on how long the child has been living elsewhere and whether someone else has made a claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in local authority care for a couple of months now. I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex is in local authority care. This is an important detail for determining eligibility.

**Does Alex spend any regular time at home with you? For example, does he come home for at least 24 hours a week, or spend at least 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home?**

The rules are different depending on whether children in care spend regular time at home with their parent.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home regularly. He's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me make sure I have the complete picture:

- Alex is 8 years old
- He's been in local authority care for a couple of months (over 8 weeks)
- He lives at the care home full-time and doesn't spend regular time at home with you
- You contribute £10 per week towards his upkeep

Based on the rules I have, when a child goes into local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you're generally no longer entitled to Child Benefit **unless** the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or spends 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row at home.

Since Alex doesn't come home regularly and is in full-time care, and given that your contributions (£10 per week) are below the Child Benefit rate (around £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child), I have sufficient information to make an assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your situation, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

When a child goes into local authority care for more than 8 weeks, parents generally lose their entitlement to Child Benefit. There are exceptions to this rule - for example, if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or at least 2 nights in a row each week at home. However, since Alex lives at the care home full-time and doesn't come home regularly, these exceptions don't apply in your case.

I understand this may be disappointing news. If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he starts spending regular time at home with you - your eligibility could change and it would be worth reassessing your situation at that time.

If you have any questions about this decision or if there's anything else I can help you with, please let me know.

Additionally, the claimant contributes £10 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is below the Child Benefit rate of approximately £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child. Even if Alex were living with someone else (rather than in care), the claimant would need to contribute at least as much as the Child Benefit payment to potentially qualify. Therefore, based on these circumstances, the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
